newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFA fines MeesPierson for trader's activities.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFA fines MeesPierson for trader's activities.

text.p: Britain's financial watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Thursday it had fined MeesPierson ICS 20,000 sterling ($31,750), plus costs of 25,560 sterling, and reprimanded the firm for failing to spot unauthorised futures trading.
The SFA also severely reprimanded Willem Van der Vorm, the trader concerned, fined him 10,000 sterling and ordered him to pay costs of 1,000 sterling.
MeesPierson is an investment bank owned by ABN AMRO which is selling the unit to Dutch/Belgian group Fortis.

Van der Vorm is an independent local trader on the floor of London's futures exchange LIFFE, the SFA said in a statement. A "local" is a self-employed person dealing on the futures or options exchange for his own account or for the account of other members of the exchange.
His trades are cleared by MeesPierson and an SFA disciplinary tribunal found that for regulatory purposes he was to be regarded as an employee of the firm.
The SFA said that before April 1991 Van der Vorm had managed the investments of two MeesPierson customers and when the rules changed after June 1991 he continued to do so.
But he was now registered as a trader by the SFA rather than its predecessor and was no longer authorised to give investment advice or manage investments for third parties.

Van der Vorm settled with the SFA and admitted he acted in breach of the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) principle on standards of integrity and fair dealing and was "in breach of MeesPierson's instruction to cease trading the accounts".
MeesPierson took its case to the SFA's disciplinary tribunal which found it had breached the SIB principle on due skill, care and diligence and the principle referring to internal organisation.
"There was a gap in MeesPierson's arrangements through which Van der Vorm's discretionary account trading was allowed to slip," the SFA said.

MeesPierson failed to detect that Van der Vorm continued to manage the accounts in question after they had twice instructed him to stop doing so. This only came to light during a routine SFA inspection, it added.
The SFA also found that MeesPierson "lacked adequate arrangements for the proper supervision of their staff" in relation to the activities of a trainee trader taken on at the request of Van der Vorm.

The trainee was not allowed to trade but did so through an account held by Van der Vorm with the knowledge of MeesPierson staff "who saw nothing untoward in his doing so and therefore did not report it up the management chain".
The tribunal found MeesPierson was responsible for supervising the trainee but that "what occurred took place because there was no adequate system for the supervision of trainees on the LIFFE floor".

Van der Vorm currently remains registered with the SFA by MeesPierson as a trader, the SFA said. MeesPierson is "principally engaged in clearing business on the LIFFE market", it added. ($1=.6299 Sterling)
